items.headline: Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin — Treasury pauses Russian oil sanctions
bullets: Numbers: Trump says Russia will supply 300k tons of diesel immediately, 500k in November, 1M after — plus 3M 'within a short period' (~4.8M tons total, ≈36M barrels). Diesel fell 3% on the news; crude barely moved (WTI ~$91.20, Brent ~$104).

Meaning: U-turn just weeks after the new Russia sanctions law — Treasury issued a temporary general license, the first Russian energy imports since 2022. IEA puts the global diesel shortfall at ~1.6M b/d, so if it all materializes this plugs ~3 weeks of the gap; traders call it too little, too late.

FX read-through: mild USD relief via the fuel-inflation channel — takes pressure off the Dec-hike premium priced into the dollar, but DXY barely budged (+0.1% to 102.24). Gold +1.5% to $4,220 on the softer dollar + lower oil.

items.headline: U Mich misses again: 46.3 vs 47.5 — but rising inflation expectations are the real read
bullets: Numbers: Oct prelim 46.3 (fcst 47.5, Sep 48.1) — third straight monthly decline; current conditions 44.7, a record low.

Meaning: consumers gloomier, but the Fed's line item moved the wrong way — 1y inflation expectations up to 4.7% (from 4.6%), 5y to 3.5% (from 3.4%), the second straight monthly rise to the highest since May.

FX read-through: stagflationary tint — softer growth expectations argue for a softer dollar, but stickier inflation expectations keep Dec hike odds alive. Net: mild USD support via the policy channel.

items.headline: Loonie sinks to 18-month low as jobs shock kills BoC hike bets
bullets: Numbers: USD/CAD 1.4275 (-0.4% Friday); touched 1.4298 intraday — weakest since April 2025; fifth straight weekly loss.
Meaning: the -68.3K jobs print keeps biting — Oct 28 hike odds down to 25% from 40%; Canada 2Y -6.8bp to 3.183%, ~161bp below the US 2Y (widest since Feb 2025).
FX read-through: market now prices BoC on hold at best — any CAD rally fights a widening rate gap. Oil softer (WTI $91.19) isn't helping.

items.next: Canada CPI Oct 21, then BoC decision Oct 28

bullets: Numbers: -68,300 jobs in September (consensus +9,200); unemployment 6.5% (from 6.4%); second straight monthly loss after -41,700 in August; 2026 YTD now -41,200; participation 64.8%, lowest in 29 years outside the pandemic; wages +2.3% y/y.

Meaning: losses led by public sector (education + healthcare -58,400), not tariffs — but this was the last jobs print before the Oct 28 BoC decision, and it kills the creeping December-hike pricing. Canada 2Y fell 8bp to ~3.20%.

FX read-through: USD/CAD up to ~1.4275 (from ~1.4225), near 52-week highs — the market is trading the miss. CAD's oil tailwind now fights a weak domestic story; the ~160bp US-Canada 2Y gap is the anchor.
